required_outcomes: Recognises that the invoice in the provider's latest email is the same Willow Homes invoice (issued 8 October 2025, £240.00 including VAT) already forwarded to the landlord on 8 October and reported paid by the landlord on 10 October.
Does not pay, approve or forward the re-sent invoice for payment a second time.
Replies to the provider that the invoice was paid by the landlord on 10 October 2025, and asks them to check their records or confirm whether the payment has been received.
acceptable_alternatives: Placing a hold on any payment against the re-sent invoice and asking the landlord to confirm the payment date or send proof of payment, as long as the provider is still told the invoice has already been paid.
Leaving the closed request closed and recording the exchange as a note, rather than reopening it.
positive_behaviours: Records in the case notes that a duplicate of the paid invoice was received and how it was handled.
Asks the landlord for payment details (date, method or reference) to help the provider trace the payment, without asking him to pay again.
Keeps the tone with the provider factual and does not suggest the invoice is disputed or that the work was unsatisfactory.
red_flags: Forwarding the re-sent invoice to the landlord as a new amount due.
Escalating to a human without first replying to the provider about the earlier payment.
prohibited_actions: Paying or approving the £240.00 invoice again.
Telling the provider that payment will be arranged.
critical_failures: Paying, approving or requesting payment of the same £240.00 invoice a second time.
